source_text: ἔχειν ἑαυτοῦ μείζονα τὸν υἱόν. 26.54 εἰπόντος γὰρ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῇ Γενέσει πρὸς τὸν Ἀβραάμ· "4τὸν υἱόν σου προσένεγκέ μοι θυσίαν"5 καὶ τοῦτο προθύμως ποιήσαντος καὶ ἐπάγειν ἐπ' αὐτὸν τὴν χεῖρα μαχαίρᾳ ὡπλισμένην μέλλοντος ἐκάλεσεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος κυρίου εἰπών· «Ἀβραάμ, μὴ ἐπιβάλῃς τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπὶ τὸ παιδάριον μήτε ποιήσῃς αὐτῷ μηθὲν κακόν. νῦν γὰρ ἔγνων, ὅτι φοβῇ σὺ τὸν θεὸν καὶ οὐκ ἐφείσω τοῦ υἱοῦ σου τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ δι' ἐμέ». 26.55 εἶτα κριοῦ πρὸς τὴν θυσίαν ἀντὶ Ἰσαὰκ εὑρεθέντος καὶ τῆς θυσίας ὑπὸ Ἀβραὰμ πληρωθείσης, τῇ μὲν γνώμῃ διὰ τοῦ παιδός, τῇ δὲ σφαγῇ διὰ τοῦ κριοῦ, «ἐκάλεσεν», φησίν, «αὐτὸν ἐκ δευτέρου ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγων· κατ' ἐμαυτοῦ ὤμοσα, λέγει κύριος, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἐποίησας τὸ πρᾶγμα καὶ οὐκ ἐφείσω τοῦ υἱοῦ σου τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ δι' ἐμέ· ἦ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς τοὺς ἀστέρας τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τὴν ἄμμον τῆς θαλάσσης· καὶ ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, ἀνθ' ὧν ὑπήκουσας τῆς ἐμῆς φωνῆς». 26.56 Ἦν δὲ οὔτε ὁ πατὴρ οὔτε μὴν λειτουργὸς ἄγγελος. 26.57 οὐ γὰρ ὀμνύει καθ' ἑαυτοῦ λειτουργὸς ἢ εὐλογεῖ ἢ λέγει· «οὐκ ἐφείσω τοῦ υἱοῦ σου τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ δι' ἐμέ»· οὐδ' ἀποστῆσαι τὴν τῷ θεῷ προσαγομένην τολμᾷ θυσίαν οὐδ' αὖ προσίεσθαι αὐτὴν ἐξουσιάζει· 26.58 ἀλλὰ ἦν ὁ τὴν θυσίαν ζητήσας μονογενὴς θεὸς λόγος χαριζόμενος τὸν μονογενῆ τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ὡς Παῦλος ἑρμηνεύει γράφων Ἑβραίοις οὑτωσί· «τῷ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐπαγγειλάμενος ὁ θεός»–ἅπερ ἐπηγγείλατό τε καὶ ἐποίησεν–»ἐπεὶ κατ' οὐδενὸς μείζονος εἶχεν ὀμόσαι, ὤμοσεν καθ' ἑαυτοῦ λέγων· ἦ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε». 26.59 καὶ Ῥωμαίοις δὲ τὸν υἱὸν αὖθις καθ' ἑαυτοῦ ὀμνύοντα ἐξηγεῖται· «πάντες γὰρ παραστησόμεθα τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ καθῶς γέγραπται· ζῶ ἐγώ, λέγει κύριος, ὅτι ἐμοὶ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολο γήσεται τῷ θεῷ». 26.60 Καὶ τὸ ἐκ δεξιῶν δὲ συγκαθέζεσθαι τῷ πατρί, ἔτι δὲ καὶ τὸ θεοφράστῳ γλώττῃ ἀναφθέγγεσθαι τὸν εὐαγγελιστὴν καθέδραν πρέπουσαν τῷ υἱῷ τὸν πατρικὸν εἶναι κόλπον εἰ μὴ σημαίνει τὸ ταυτούσιον καὶ ὁμότιμον καὶ τὸ χρῆναι σὺν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ προσκυνεῖσθαι τὸν μονογενῆ θεὸν καὶ υἱόν, ἀλλά–κατὰ ἄνθρωπον οὐ δέον ἐκδέχεσθαι γρὴ τὰ περὶ θεοῦ γεγραμμένα–μείζων καὶ ἐνδοξότερος κατ' αὐτούς ἐστιν ὁ ἐκ δεξιῶν, ὁ τὸν θεϊκὸν ἄφατον κόλπον ὡς τὸν χερουβικὸν ἔχων πολυῶπα θρόνον. 26.61 ὃ μὴ γένοιτο εἰπεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς ἀρρητοτάτης καὶ γαληνοτάτης τριάδος. 26.62 ὁ μὲν γὰρ ∆αυὶδ ᾄδει περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐν ρθʹ ψαλμῷ· «εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου»· 26.63 ὁ δὲ Παῦλος Ἑβραίοις ὑφηγεῖται· «ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ φέρων τε τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, καθαρισμὸν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ποιησάμενος, ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τῆς μεγαλωσύνης ἐν 29 ὑψηλοῖς»· 26.64 ὁ δὲ εὐαγγελιστής· «ὁ μονογενὴς θεὸς ὁ ὢν ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ τοῦ πατρός, αὐτὸ ἐξηγήσατο». 27.ν Ὁμοίως θεολογία περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ, ὅτι «ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικεῖ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος» καὶ ὅτι «θεὸς μέγας» καί «ἐπὶ πάντων», «πρὸς ὃν οὐ λογισθήσε ται ἕτερος» καί «ἀληθινὸς θεός» καὶ «ζωὴ αἰώνιος» καί «μόνος δεσπότης» καί «μόνος θαυματουργός» καί «ὕψιστος» καί «βασιλεύς» καί «ἐξουσια στής» καί «πάντα ἐν πᾶσι Χριστός» καί τὰ λοιπά. 27.1 Τοσαῦτα μὲν περὶ τούτων ἤρκει· οὐκ ἠρεμοῦσι δὲ οἱ τῶν θείων μύσται καὶ τὰ τῆς προνοητικωτάτης πάντων τριάδος ζηλοῦντες ἄλλ' ἔτι ὑψηλά· καὶ οἷα περὶ τοῦ πατρός, τοιαῦτα καὶ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ θεολογοῦσιν, ὅτι «ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικεῖ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος» καὶ ὅτι «θεὸς μέγας» καί «ἐπὶ πάντων», «πρὸς ὃν οὐ λογισθήσεται ἕτερος» καί «ἀληθινὸς θεός» καί «ζωὴ αἰώνιος» καί «φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν» καί «μόνος δεσπότης» καί «μόνος ὕψιστος» καί «μόνος θαυματοποιός» καί «βασιλεὺς μέγας» καί «κύριος πάντων» καί

pass_b_english: … have anyone greater than himself: the Son. For in Genesis God said to Abraham, “Offer me your son as a sacrifice” (Genesis 22:2). Abraham did this readily, and he was about to bring his hand down upon him, armed with a knife, when an angel of the Lord called to him and said, “Abraham, do not lay your hand on the boy, and do him no harm at all. For now I know that you fear God, and for my sake you have not spared your beloved son” (Genesis 22:12).

Then a ram was found for the sacrifice in place of Isaac, and Abraham completed the sacrifice: in intention through the boy, in the slaughter through the ram. And “the angel of the Lord,” it says, “called him a second time from heaven, saying: ‘By myself I have sworn, says the Lord: because you have done this thing, and for my sake have not spared your beloved son, I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand of the sea; and in you all the nations shall be blessed, because you obeyed my voice’” (Genesis 22:15-18).

Yet this was neither the Father nor, for that matter, a ministering angel. For a servant does not swear by himself, or bless, or say, “For my sake you have not spared your beloved son.” Nor does he dare to halt a sacrifice that is being offered to God, nor, again, has he authority to accept it. No: the one who asked for the sacrifice was the only-begotten God, the Word, who granted Abraham his only son. So Paul explains when he writes to the Hebrews in this way: “For when God made his promise to Abraham” (the things he both promised and performed), “since he had no one greater by whom to swear, he swore by himself, saying, ‘I will surely bless you’” (Hebrews 6:13-14). And to the Romans, too, he explains that it is the Son who once more swears by himself: “For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ, as it is written: ‘As I live, says the Lord, to me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall confess to God’” (Romans 14:10-11).

Then there is his sitting with the Father at his right hand; and, besides, the evangelist’s declaring, with a tongue that spoke the words of God, that the seat fitting for the Son is the Father’s bosom. If these do not signify sameness of substance and equal honour, and that the only-begotten God and Son must be worshipped together with the Father and his Spirit, then (if we must take what is written about God in a human way, as we should not) by their reckoning the one at the right hand is greater and more glorious, the one who has the divine, ineffable bosom for his throne, like the many-eyed throne of the cherubim. God forbid that this be said of the most ineffable and most serene Trinity! For David sings of the Father in Psalm 110: “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand’” (Psalm 110:1). Paul instructs the Hebrews: “Who, being the radiance of the Father’s glory and the imprint of his hypostasis, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had made purification for sins, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high” (Hebrews 1:3). And the evangelist says: “The only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made it known” (John 1:18).

Likewise the theology concerning the Son: that “in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead”; that he is “great God” and “over all,” the one “with whom no other shall be compared,” “true God” and “eternal life,” “only Master,” “only worker of wonders,” “Most High,” “King,” and “Sovereign”; that “Christ is all in all”; and the rest.

So much on these matters was enough. But the initiates of divine things, zealous for all that belongs to the Trinity, whose providence is over all, do not rest; they pursue still other lofty truths. What they declare of the Father as God, they declare of the Son as well: that “in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead” (Colossians 2:9); that he is “great God” (Titus 2:13) and “over all” (Romans 9:5), the one “with whom no other shall be compared” (Baruch 3:35), “true God” and “eternal life” (1 John 5:20), “the true light” (John 1:9), “only Master” (Jude 4), “only Most High,” “only worker of wonders,” “great King,” “Lord of all” (Acts 10:36), and …

choices.issue: Misread opening, garbled clauses, dropped clause, chapter title merged, abbreviated references
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English opened 'He has the Son as greater for himself', reversing Didymus' point (the negative stands at the end of the previous section: the Son has no one greater than himself, as Hebrews 6:13 shows). In 26.57 it gave 'I will not withhold' for 'you did not spare' and 'offer it again' for προσίεσθαι (to accept it). It broke off 26.59 with 'And the sitting at the right hand of the…' and lost that clause; the rest of 26.60 was garbled ('the Evangelist uses the term bosom appearing to the Son … unless it signifies the same and of equal nature'). The chapter title 27.ν was run into 27.1 as if it were text. References: 'Gen 22:2', 'Gen 22:12', 'Heb 6:13-14', 'Rom 14:10-11' written in full; 'Gen 22:16-18' made Genesis 22:15-18 (the quotation starts with 'called him a second time', verse 15); Titus 2:13, Romans 9:5, Baruch 3:35, 1 John 5:20, John 1:9, Jude 4 and Acts 10:36 added. Brackets [the one swearing], [the words], [says], [states] removed.

choices.english: … have anyone greater than himself: the Son.
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence; the negative (μὴ) and Paul's 'crying out' close the previous section. Only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
The digits 4 and 5 around Genesis 22:2 are footnote markers in the copy-text; debris, skipped.

choices.english: in intention through the boy, in the slaughter through the ram
choices.why: Didymus' balanced phrase kept: Abraham's sacrifice was complete in will with Isaac, in deed with the ram.

choices.english: who granted Abraham his only son
choices.why: τὸν μονογενῆ here is Isaac (Hebrews 11:17 calls him μονογενής); the Word gave him back to Abraham by stopping the sacrifice.

choices.english: with a tongue that spoke the words of God
choices.why: θεόφραστος: uttered by God; said of the evangelist's inspired speech.

choices.why: A parenthesis that makes the absurd conclusion depend on a human reading of Scripture; γρὴ is a misprint for χρή.
